note: The Duchy of Spoleto — a Lombard duchy in central Italy that survived the Carolingian conquest of the main Lombard kingdom (774) — maintained a complex, often hostile relationship with the papacy and a gradually evolving one with the Carolingian/imperial overlords. Situated between Rome and northern Italy, Spoleto periodically threatened the papacy, served as a buffer against other Lombard principalities, and was granted to various imperial supporters. Pope Innocent III incorporated Spoleto into the Papal States (1198) through a combination of political maneuvering and imperial weakness during the Staufen succession crisis.

_quarry.structural_significance: Spoleto's incorporation into the Papal States by Innocent III represents the high point of papal territorial expansion; the duchy's absorption eliminates the last autonomous Lombard territorial entity in central Italy and completes the Papal States' geographic coherence
